move: browser window rises, page scrolls, each block lifts in as it enters
how: A 900px browser window with an editorial article (serif headline, hero image, paragraphs, two-up images, pull quote) sits on a warm grey stage. The window enters with from y:120/opacity:0 over the first 18% (expo.out), the nav fades and the two headline lines rise via yPercent:110 line-masks (expo.out, stagger 0.1) at 7%. From 26% to 90% the .doc translates y to -(scrollHeight - viewport) with power1.inOut while a thin scrollbar thumb tracks it; each .r block gets a from y:44/opacity:0 expo.out reveal timed by numerically inverting the scroll ease so it fires when the block crosses the lower third of the viewport, and images settle from scale 1.2 to 1 while their .im layers drift yPercent:-6 for parallax. At 91% the window drops out with y:140/opacity:0 expo.in.
adapt: Replace the URL bar text, masthead, headline lines, byline, body copy and the three background images (sunset/ocean/aurora); keep the 0.9s window entrance, the 3.2s power1.inOut scroll and the 0.7s expo.out block reveals. Article length changes the scroll distance automatically since it is measured from scrollHeight.
port: mount(el, shot) builds the window/doc markup inside el from shot strings and image URLs; animate(el, shot, D) measures doc.scrollHeight - view.clientHeight after mount, builds the same timeline with times as fractions of D (window in 0-0.18, scroll 0.26-0.9, exit at 0.91) and returns it. All selectors must be scoped with el.querySelector; the ease-inversion loop for reveal timing works unchanged; images are preloaded with fx.wait so the engine needs an equivalent decode wait.
caveats: reveal timing depends on layout measurement (offsetTop/scrollHeight), so fonts must be loaded before building
